title: Chosen for the radio 'Children's Hour' in Atlanta
summary: At school in Atlanta he is picked for a children's radio show because he sings like Morton Downey, Paul Robeson and Kate Smith; rehearsal for a royal visit begins.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: I was about five, about five years old, you see. And -- so we went to Atlanta, Georgia, and my mother's mother, you see. And I was entered into another school, public school, Davis T. Howard, you see. And they had a procedure in that grade, first grade, which is called kindergarten, right? Like when you get up to the head of the class, it would be about eight of us in the head of the class, whenever you get there, but you would get to the head of the class by doing some kind of compositioning.

And they used to have people come there observing the head of the class, and one time they had some people from radio, 'Children's Hour'; they came there. And each one of us in the head of the class would have to get up and read something from our composition.

So, that time, I was into singing, like -- so I read something from my composition, and they wanted to know if I sang or did anything, what did I do besides -- they liked my voice or something, body. So I told them that I had been taking singing lessons, you know. And -- all right -- so they --
Now, you were taking singing lessons --
-- along with your mother when she went to her classes?

No, no, that was after we came -- left Fitzgerald, Georgia. See, this was in Atlanta, Georgia, which was a city. It was called the Little New York City, I mean at that time, but it was still Atlanta. And so they asked me what kind of singing did I do. So I -- luckily I could say that I sang like some famous people at that time, like Mort Downey. He was very famous. And another I did, like a little Paul Robeson, you know, but as a child, you see, I could do bass voice like a little bit. And it's kind of, you know, that's what they wanted, and they needed that kind of thing.

So I told them I sang like Kate Smith, you know, and this 'When the Moon Comes Over the Mountain' and so on. So anyhow I was chosen for the 'Children's Hour', right? So now, once the -- that's the American Broadcasting Company.

Once they chose, you see, they would continue your education, but you would get more. You could go to dancing school. You could go to -- you know, learn a lot of different things that you wouldn't ordinarily learn in the first grade of a school, see.

So it went on pretty good for a while, about a week and a half. So -- until this announcer came one day -- he said, as -- he said that the royal family was coming there with their children, see, because in a radio station there you never have any audience. It's just the microphone and the performers, you see. So they -- being the royal family, naturally they come up into the studio and so on, and it was like a private audience, you see.

But the fellow wanted us to rehearse what we were going to do, each child, you see. So now, when it came to my time, I had to -- I sang -- I had to sing that Morton Downey and, like I said, a little bit of Paul Robeson. But I didn't know all the song, the words on the Paul Robeson song.
So he said, 'Well, you wouldn't have to do that. Do you do anything else?' So I says, 'Well, I sing like Kate Smith.'
Now, he was a new announcer. So he wasn't familiar with the children's performing.
